title.narrative: Activity under preparation Support to Anti Money Laundering/Counter Financing Terrorism Activities in Mauritius - SAMLM

description.narrative: The overall objective of the SAMLM project is to support the adoption of enhanced measures aimed at preventing money laundering and cutting off access to financing for terrorist organisations and individuals in the Republic of Mauritius. This involves strengthening compliance with the recommendations framework set by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), the European Union (EU) Anti-Money Laundering/Counter-Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) regime, and relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions.In February 2020, Mauritius was placed on the FATF's "Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring list and blacklisted by the EU as a High-Risk jurisdiction for AML/CFT. This required Mauritius to implement several reforms. By October 2021, Mauritius successfully exited the FATF's enhanced scrutiny list ahead of schedule, prompting the EU to also delist Mauritius.Mauritius is scheduled for a next cycle of evaluation by ESAMLAAG in 2027.The proposed programme `Support to the Anti Money Laundering/Counter Financing Terrorism Activities for Mauritius (SAMLM)¿ will aim at helping Mauritius to prepare for the next round of evaluation.This program builds on the EU AML/CFT Global Facility's support since 2019. It will expand on past successes to tackle new AML/CFT/CPF challenges. The SAMLM program outlines strategies to enhance coordination, increase training and capacity-building, and foster stakeholder cooperation. It emphasizes innovation and adaptation to changes in the AML/CFT landscape to ensure sustainable outcomes. The programme will ensure collaboration with the new EU SECFIN programme devoted to fighting illicit financial flows.The action is also in line with the EU Global Gateway. To incentivize private-sector buy-in into Global Gateway objectives and activities, the stability of the financial sector needs to be ensured to reduce financing costs. Combating money laundering and terrorism financing ensures the stability of the financial sector thereby remaining a reliable and clean financial jurisdiction and thus facilitating a conducive investment climate.
